title: Listener port
text: RelayGate 1.0 listens on TCP port 8080 by default. Set RELAY_PORT to change the listener port. Restart the service after changing RELAY_PORT.

title: Authentication configuration
text: RelayGate 1.0 uses a single service token configured with RELAY_TOKEN. Requests must send that token in the X-Relay-Token header. An absent or mismatched token returns HTTP 401. Do not put the token in URLs.

title: Health checks
text: RelayGate 1.0 exposes GET /healthz for liveness. HTTP 200 means the process is alive; it does not confirm downstream connectivity. Check downstream connectivity separately before sending traffic.

title: Retry behavior
text: RelayGate 1.0 does not retry failed downstream requests automatically. A caller may retry a read-only request with bounded exponential backoff. Do not automatically replay a write unless the downstream service supports idempotency.

title: Logging and troubleshooting
text: RelayGate 1.0 writes operational logs to standard output. Set RELAY_LOG_LEVEL=debug temporarily when investigating a failed connection, then restore info. Redact service tokens before sharing any logs.

title: Downstream timeout
text: RelayGate 1.0 has a fixed downstream request timeout of 10 seconds. Version 1.0 has no environment variable to change this timeout. A timed-out downstream request returns HTTP 504.

title: Trusted reverse proxy
text: RelayGate 1.0 trusts forwarded client headers only when RELAY_TRUST_PROXY=true. Enable this setting only behind a reverse proxy that removes untrusted incoming forwarded headers. The default is false.

title: Configuration persistence
text: RelayGate 1.0 reads environment configuration at startup. Configuration changes require a service restart. RelayGate 1.0 does not store a request queue; pending requests are lost if the process exits.

title: Listener port
text: RelayGate 2.0 listens on TCP port 9090 by default. Set RELAY_LISTEN_PORT to change the listener port. RELAY_PORT is ignored in version 2.0. Restart the service after changing RELAY_LISTEN_PORT.

title: Authentication configuration
text: RelayGate 2.0 uses a service token configured with RELAY_API_KEY. Requests must send Authorization: Bearer followed by the configured token. X-Relay-Token and RELAY_TOKEN are not accepted in version 2.0. An invalid token returns HTTP 401.

title: Liveness and readiness
text: RelayGate 2.0 exposes GET /health/live for liveness and GET /health/ready for readiness. Readiness returns HTTP 200 only after a successful downstream probe within the last 30 seconds; otherwise it returns HTTP 503. The old /healthz route returns HTTP 404.

title: Retry behavior
text: RelayGate 2.0 retries downstream GET and HEAD requests once after a connection failure, with a 250 millisecond delay. It does not automatically retry POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. Caller retries must remain bounded and account for the built-in retry.

title: Logging and troubleshooting
text: RelayGate 2.0 writes JSON operational logs to standard output. Set RELAY_LOG_LEVEL=debug temporarily to investigate issues. Log entries include request_id for correlating requests. Redact Authorization headers and API keys before sharing logs.

title: Configurable downstream timeout
text: RelayGate 2.0 defaults to a downstream timeout of 15 seconds. Set RELAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to an integer from 1 through 60 to change it, then restart. An invalid value prevents startup. A timed-out request returns HTTP 504.

title: Trusted reverse proxy
text: RelayGate 2.0 requires RELAY_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS to contain an explicit comma-separated CIDR allowlist before trusting forwarded client headers. With an empty allowlist, forwarded headers are ignored. RELAY_TRUST_PROXY is not supported in version 2.0.

title: Configuration persistence
text: RelayGate 2.0 reads environment configuration at startup and requires a restart after changes. It does not persist a request queue. Drain in-flight requests before restarting; the graceful-shutdown window is 20 seconds.

title: Queue shutdown API
text: Queue.shutdown() and queue.ShutDown are not part of the Python 3.12 queue API. They were introduced in Python 3.13. Code that relies on those APIs requires Python 3.13 or later.
source_label: Python documentation; API marked added in 3.13

title: Task completion and join
text: Queue.join() waits for all queued work to be marked complete. Each put() increases the unfinished-task count; each task_done() decreases it. Calling task_done() too many times raises ValueError. A queue being empty does not by itself establish that all retrieved work finished.

title: Queue shutdown API
text: Python 3.13 adds Queue.shutdown(immediate=False). It prevents new puts and unblocks blocked producers with queue.ShutDown. Existing queued work can drain normally; after the queue is empty, get() raises ShutDown. With immediate=True, the queue is drained immediately and blocked consumers are also unblocked with ShutDown.

title: Task completion and join
text: Normally, Queue.join() waits until queued tasks have matching task_done() calls. Queue.shutdown(immediate=True) can unblock join() even when work was not completed. A returned join() after immediate shutdown is therefore not proof that all queued work finished. Prefer normal draining when completion accounting must be preserved.
